technical_and_design_decisions: Define a common Admin SPI contract for module status retrieval, module listing, and status mapping, with Receptor and Cloud Controller as interchangeable implementations.
Create a permanent shared repository/package location for SPI interfaces, implementations, and supporting models so both production code and tests consume the same contract.
Introduce a minimal Module Registry abstraction that separates module discovery and metadata lookup from the underlying Receptor, Cloud Controller, or Eureka mechanism.
Use dependency injection and runtime profiles to select the appropriate Admin SPI implementation for local JAR execution, Cloud Foundry deployment, and other supported deployment modes.
Use Eureka as the service registry for module self-registration, module-name lookup, and metadata/state storage.
Retain Spring Boot's spring.application.name as the default module identity while supporting an explicit module name property for searches and registration.
Represent module metadata in Eureka instance metadata fields, with a documented mapping for module name, descriptor, version, deployment identity, and health/status information.
Implement adapters around existing Receptor, Cloud Controller, and Eureka clients rather than introducing new transport protocols.
Prefer backward-compatible interfaces and configuration defaults so existing module deployment and administration behavior continues to work when the new SPI is not explicitly configured.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD codebase, build system, deployment abstractions, Receptor client, Cloud Controller client, and Eureka client libraries are available and functional.
The increment is an initial production-capable implementation, not a complete redesign of Spring XD deployment or service discovery.
Existing authentication, authorization, network connectivity, and credentials for Receptor, Cloud Controller, and Eureka are handled by the surrounding platform or existing configuration.
The specification does not define exact existing interfaces, so compatible method signatures will be added or adapted around the stated getStatus, listModules, and status-map APIs.
Cloud Foundry support targets the currently used Cloud Controller API and deployment model; compatibility with every historical Cloud Foundry version is out of scope.
Eureka registration uses standard application registration and metadata capabilities; no Eureka server changes are required.
Health metrics are limited to the status and metadata exposed by the underlying platform clients and Eureka registrations.

Testing includes unit tests, mocked client tests, and focused integration tests using test doubles or embedded services where practical; a full multi-platform deployment test environment is not assumed.
The developer performs analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, code review preparation, and defect correction personally.
Effort is expressed in work-hours and excludes elapsed waiting time for external environments, credentials, or infrastructure.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing Spring XD administration, deployment, module descriptor, profile, and discovery code; resolve API boundaries; document the target architecture and compatibility constraints for all user stories.

activities.activity_name: Permanent SPI repository and common contract
activities.activity_description: Create or reorganize the permanent package/module location for Admin SPI interfaces, shared status models, module keys, descriptors, and common exceptions; update build dependencies and package references.
Implement the initial Module Registry abstraction and its domain model, including module lookup, listing, status retrieval, and status-map operations needed by the Admin SPI implementations.

Implement the Receptor-backed Admin SPI, mapping Receptor module queries and health/status responses into the common module descriptor and ModuleStatus model, including error handling and configuration.
Implement the Cloud Controller-backed Admin SPI for module deployment status, listing, health-related information, descriptor mapping, status aggregation, and platform-client failure handling.

Add profile and deployment-mode configuration so the appropriate SPI implementation is automatically selected for java -jar admin, Cloud Foundry, and the supported local/container deployment mode; verify default and override behavior.
Add module startup registration and shutdown handling, populate Eureka registration metadata, and ensure installed modules expose the identity and deployment information required by the Admin SPI.

Add configuration and model support for a module name distinct from spring.application.name, implement name-based lookup and filtering, and preserve the Boot application name as the fallback identity.

Implement storage and retrieval of module metadata and current state through Eureka, including conversion between Eureka instances and module descriptors/statuses and integration with the Module Registry.

Create tests for common SPI contracts, registry behavior, Receptor and Cloud Controller adapters, profile selection, Eureka registration, metadata mapping, name search, failure cases, and backward-compatible defaults.
Update dependency management, sample configuration, deployment/profile documentation, API documentation, migration notes, and developer guidance for adding or testing future SPI implementations.
Run the complete build and representative deployment/discovery scenarios, diagnose integration defects, refine mappings and configuration, and perform final cleanup and release-readiness checks.
